title: Lava Lake Within Halema`uma`u Vent (B-roll)
date: 2011-09-09 (page date; activity shown is from early June 2011)
place: Lava lake deep inside the Halemaʻumaʻu vent cavity, Kīlauea summit, Hawaiʻi Volcanoes NP, Hawaiʻi
audio: natural (kept, aac); original is field audio of the vent (roar/hiss) - nobody has listened closely, check before use
notes: Looking down into the glowing lava lake: a bright orange stream of lava pours in from upper-centre and runs diagonally to lower-right (x~0.45-0.8), black crust plates with glowing cracks swirl around it, dark rubble wall in the lower right (x>0.75, rising to x>0.9 at the top). Whole 14 s is one steady shot; slight camera drift. Best seconds 0-10. Small white 'USGS' bug in the bottom-right corner (x~0.86-0.99, y~0.95) - outside the centre square, cropped away. No people. LOW RES: source is 850x480 29.97 fps, upscaled to 1920x1080 - looks soft. Is a lava lake, not a fountain, but it is still Kīlauea (top3 used Kīlauea lava fountains).
fact_en: For scale, the lava lake is about 150 meters (164 yards) wide here. The lava stream plunges into the lava lake, disrupting the crust in a chaotic fashion.
